name: HBM Memory Snapshot
description: Whole-device HBM snapshot inspector for allocator fragmentation: capacity/address map, a zoomed fragment window drawn as an oblique-projection 3D container with the pending allocation suspended above it (too wide to drop into any free gap), allocation lifetimes, stack details, and source/timeline navigation.
useWhen: explaining why an allocation failed while total free HBM still exists
inspecting whole-device GB-scale allocation lifetimes and Python stacks
linking a memory snapshot to Timeline and source code
requiredApis: window.PtoHbmMemorySnapshot.render(container, snapshot, options) returning { resize, destroy, select }
allowedOverrides: snapshot summary, allocation blocks, fragmentationMap address segments, category labels, stack text
notes: The 3D container uses cabinet oblique projection, not the true isometric of config-relation-capacity's buildBox: here the measured quantity is address length along a horizontal axis, so x must stay horizontal and unscaled for two spans to be comparable by eye. The shading grammar (top brightest / front / right darkest), dashed wireframe = capacity, and --danger for the part that does not fit are shared with that pattern.
fragmentationMap is required for the container graphic; without it the scene degenerates to an empty container.
forbiddenOverrides: using this pattern for UB/L1/L0C kernel-local reuse; use memory-reuse-viewer
mutating generated allocation DOM directly instead of updating the snapshot payload
hard-coding product chrome colors outside the pattern
agentReuseRule: Load pattern.css and pattern.js, pass a GB-scale memory snapshot with summary.capacityGB and lifetimes, and use callbacks for Timeline/source navigation. Use memory-reuse-viewer for on-chip tensor reuse.
